title: Agent-bench run 4: the historical 60-trial evaluation after the decision contract
summary: The 60-trial evaluation (4 cells x 5 tasks x 3 trials) after the strict chip.work-decision.v1 contract: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemma under the canonical schema versus a permissive object format.

tasks.B: config discovery with a distractor (2750 vs 9000)
tasks.E: change MAX_RETRIES and pass the tests

results.gemma_canonical_vs_permissive: canonical: in 12/15 trials the first reply was a valid `complete` with no observations (refused); first replies: schema -> complete with 0 reads, schema-flat -> request_capability without a capability, object -> project.list
results.local_object_failures: B a duplicate "query_path" key 3/3; C ungrounded; E token or call timeouts

limitations: no run isolates the individual sentences of the contract
the schema is not shown to help any provider
local task D passes only vacuously

needs: a local model server (LM Studio / oMLX / llama.cpp) on the author's machine

comparability: Agent-bench tasks A-E (small synthetic fixtures, inspect and change kinds), 3 trials per cell, max_output_tokens 8192, 120 s calls; not comparable with the hard-task suite (different tasks, budgets and code revision). This is the only multi-provider 60-trial evaluation; it is a historical baseline, not a comparison point for bake-off rates.
